label: Hotel-level client requests
purpose: Client hotel API traffic counted per hotel requested: every hotel asked for in a request is one hotel request, answered OK (available) or KO, with the room/rate combinations returned and a hotel-level look-to-book. The cube for traffic by hotel, hotel country/region/city and supplier code.
grain: Hotel request lines (one per hotel asked for in each client request) aggregated per request day, customer, hotel, request type, availability type and travel window.
use_for: which hotels, hotel countries or cities clients request most
hotel-level availability rate (OK/KO) by hotel, country or supplier code
hotel-level look-to-book by hotel country or customer
demand by travel window (days before check-in)
not_for: requests sent to suppliers (Statistics Hotel Supplier)

coverage.note: Daily from 2026-08-17 to yesterday; 2026-08-21 and 2026-08-22 have no data.

dates.label: Request date
dates.meaning: Day the client request was received (the cube's main date).

measures.name: [% Hotel Requests KO]
measures.label: Hotel-level KO rate
measures.definition: Hotel requests answered KO as a share of all hotel requests ([Hotel Requests KO] / [Total Hotel Requests]).

measures.name: [% Hotel Requests OK]
measures.label: Hotel-level OK rate
measures.definition: Hotel requests answered OK as a share of all hotel requests ([Hotel Requests OK] / [Total Hotel Requests]).

measures.name: [% L2B]
measures.label: Hotel-level look-to-book %
measures.definition: Bookings as a share of hotel requests: the inverse of [L2B], a tiny percentage.

measures.name: [Avg Combinations]
measures.label: Combinations per hotel request
measures.definition: Average combinations returned per hotel request ([Combinations] / [Total Hotel Requests]).

measures.name: [Avg Days Travel Window]
measures.label: Average travel window (days)
measures.definition: Meant as the average days between request and check-in.
measures.hidden_reason: broken: returns about 0 days (even inside the '91 to 180 Days' band) and negative values; use the 'Travel Window' breakdown

measures.name: [Combinations]
measures.label: Combinations returned
measures.definition: Number of room/board/rate combinations (priced options) returned for the hotels requested.

measures.name: [Hotel Requests KO]
measures.label: Hotel requests KO
measures.definition: Hotel request lines answered KO: no availability or an error for that hotel.

measures.name: [Hotel Requests OK]
measures.label: Hotel requests OK
measures.definition: Hotel request lines answered OK: the hotel returned availability.
measures.notes: Its share (63%) matches Statistics Zone [% Hotels Results] (62%).

measures.name: [L2B]
measures.label: Hotel-level look-to-book
measures.definition: Hotel requests per booking (about 2 million hotel requests for each booking).
measures.notes: Different denominator from Statistics History Client [L2B] (requests per booking): never compare the two.

measures.name: [Total Hotel Requests]
measures.label: Hotel-level requests
measures.definition: Number of hotel request lines: one per hotel asked for in each client request (a 20-hotel search counts 20). About 5 times the number of searches and close to Statistics Zone [Hotels Requests]. Not the number of searches.
measures.notes: Sep 2026: 26.0 bn here vs 25.0 bn Statistics Zone [Hotels Requests] and 4.7 bn searches.

rules: [Total Hotel Requests] counts one line per hotel asked for in each request (about 5x the number of searches, close to Statistics Zone [Hotels Requests]). Never report it as searches: searches are Statistics Zone [Total Requests].
[Hotel Requests OK] + [Hotel Requests KO] = [Total Hotel Requests].
[L2B] and [% L2B] here are hotel-level (hotel requests per booking), not comparable with Statistics History Client [L2B]. Never add them; they are blank when grouped by request type.
[Avg Days Travel Window] is broken (about 0 days); use the 'Travel Window' breakdown for how far ahead clients request.
Data starts 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-21/22 are missing: flag periods that include them as partial.
'Customers'[Customer Manager] and 'Hotels'[Account Manager] are mostly n/a; use 'Customers'[Account Manager].
Hotel, city and region lists are very long: always ask for a top N.
Use the cube's measures only; never SUM a column.

review.question: Should "hotels requested" stay Statistics Zone [Hotels Requests], with Statistics Hotel Client [Total Hotel Requests] used only when the question needs hotel-level detail (by hotel, hotel country/city, supplier code)?
review.why: Both count hotels asked for inside searches (Sep 2026: 25.0 bn vs 26.0 bn, about 4% apart). Statistics Zone has the longer history (from 2026-07-18) and the search context; Hotel Client is the only one with hotel-level detail and starts 2026-08-17.
